notes.title: Bug fix for notification sound randomly not sounding
notes.notes:
A small bug fix thanks to Jojomo who noticed that the exercise notification sound sometimes didn't sound for the end of exercises during strength exercises.

In the end, found a notification bell script that was not enabled in the Squat Hold exercise's code. For example, if WIde Grip Push Ups transitioned into Squat Holds the end of the Wide Grip Push Ups notification sound would not sound.

This should be fixed now.  A high five to Jojomo for spotting that and letting me know.

notes.title: Bug Fix
notes.notes:
Perry kindly let me know about a bug that was happening in the last build.

The bug I would guess has been caused by switching compilers, so I have rolled back to using the VM compiler instead of the YYC compiler.

notes.title: 6 More Awards Added, Total Calorie Count & ESC Key Patch
notes.notes:
* Crafozura suggested adding a total calorie count over the span of the game life. This has been added now. You can navigate to Settings > Calorie Count and see the total calories shown in the bottom left, or alternately mouse over the new calorie amount awards.

* 5 new awards added to the awards screen linked to how many total calories burned over the game life.

* Luke Puke requested that the awards be somehow linked to Steam awards, so a Steam Award has been added that unlocks after all the 48 in-game awards are unlocked and turned to yellow. (Not an easy Steam award to get, especially as the 100 workout in-game award is a tough one to crack.)

* Crafozura requested that the ESC key whilst in mid workout be changed to show the pause menu instead of exiting the game totally. As if the ESC key gets pressed accidentally it can wipe out progress within that workout causing the player to start over again. This has been changed now.

notes.title: Stopwatch graphic added for clearer indication of stance / direction changes
notes.notes:
* Added a stopwatch graphic for clearer graphical indication of stance / direction changes.
* Improved the exercise screen's UI panel with new graphics.

I will keep on adding better UI graphics with each update, as requested by players.

When I first made the graphics I used a UI graphics resource pack + Gamemaker's pixel graphics draw tools. Which would be okay for a retro pixel game, but not this game. This time I'm using Inkscape to make vector graphics from scratch which are a lot clearer.

Still coding in the sprite speed control - it is about 50% done already, so not long now . . .

notes.title: Bug fix for transitions not showing
notes.notes:
Bug fix for a bug that caused transitions not to show. I am fairly confident I found the bug and it should be stable now.

It was a weird bug as I tested the game for 5 hours, then in the morning went to play the game and found a glaring glitch.

Please tell me if there are any other issues, but it should be okay now, hopefully . . . if not I can roll back to a previous build.

Thank you astron82 for flagging this up.

notes.title: Rolled Back to Previous Build/Version Due to a Bug/Glitch
notes.notes: Just temporarily rolled back to the previous version, as there was a bug that didn't show on testing. I will get busy fixing this and will re-release the update for 'no rest after rest periods' as a more stable version.

notes.title: No Transitions After Rest Periods Patch
notes.notes:
* Transition periods after rest periods have been taken out, as players can see the exercise coming up, so the extra rest period was overkill.

This was from another one of Astron82's helpful suggestions.

notes.title: Less Dings + Small Requested Changes to Transitions
notes.notes:
Just the first of a few patches that will go up based on astron82's observations to make the transitions better. More to come . . .

* Second ding/alert sound dulled down so as not to ding players out.
* Green transition bar changed to red and text changed to 'Get ready'.
* Small graphics glitch fixed that was showing 'Advanced' text on the level button too brightly.

notes.title: The next update will be focused on transitions between exercises
notes.notes:
Many thanks for all player feedback and ideas. There is one suggestion that has been put forward by players multiple times, which is:

[h1]'Implement a transition / time transition between exercises as players are losing 2-5 seconds transitioning from one exercise to another'.[/h1] . . So this needs to be added asap. I hear you.

So I have moved this firmly to the front, to be seen in the next major 1.9 update. There may be a few small fixes /  minor updates /improvements in between put out as minor patches,  but I'm targeting this request for 1.9.

I totally agree. I am onto it and already plan to put extra hours into remedying this.

So happy that a lot of players like the concept and are enjoying the game. I have just got to knuckle down and get that update out now for transitions / time to change exercise stance.

So fired up to get this done. Thanks again for making me aware of this crucial update.

notes.title: Patch for better yellow 'tips' text visibility
notes.notes: Put in a background behind the yellow text to make the yellow 'tips' scrolling text easier for players to read.

notes.title: Bug fix for mysterious lost of total workout time
notes.notes:
Thanks to Moo again for giving me another valuable heads up. Moo said that his progress showed that he'd worked out for around 7 hours but that he knew he'd worked out for close to 11 hours.

To fix this bug I first checked all the timers in the game which appeared to be fine. So I went over the save system and found the bug there. So I restructured the save system and the bug is no more.

The bug kind of made players workout more than they needed to in order to unlock rooms and ranks, so it is maybe the only computer bug in the world that has helped people to get fitter lol.

notes.title: Fixed bug where player progress was reset to zero after game engine update
notes.notes:
After the 1.4 version was uploaded, to my complete horror, all player progress and unlocks were set to zero . . . luckily Moo made me aware of this and now this is fixed.

The bug came about after a major update to the game engine I'm using (Gamemaker 2) when I had to rename the project again - but the project's name was slightly different to the original project's name, so the file path to the INI save file was thrown out.

I should have picked this up on testing the build, but I mistakenly thought that I had personally reset my own progress recently.

Sorry about that. Everything should be back to normal now.

notes.title: More content and improvements coming in the September update
notes.notes:
Updates for build 1.3:

* 10 tutorials added.
* Small graphics bug fixed (a thin strip of the tutorial was left over in the blue room but fixed now).
* File optimisation, changing all WAV music files to OGG files for less memory usage.
* PNG file optimisation.
* Circle crunches reanimated with an improved technique.

Firstly, thank you to Moo this month for some great suggestions for the game and also giving me a heads up on the Steam achievements not kicking in. I will work on getting the Steam achievements working, so will look into this.

I'll be honest here and say straight off the bat that this isn't a great update, as I took a holiday this month and also hit a snag. The game hit the 2GB RAM limit for 32 bit games recently, so I reduced the file sizes of the the music files by around 40%, thinking that this would free up memory for new content. . . . But to my dismay it oddly had no effect.

So, in a nutshell, I could only add some of the new content this month. The rest of the content I will add in a September update, when I overcome this snag.

It seems as though the textures (graphics and images) have their own memory limit . . . perhaps? So I will work on externally loading the images next to hopefully overcome this barrier. Sorry that this update is far from great, but I hope to make up for this in the September update, where I will try to get all tutorials completed and up.

Still keeping positive though, just a snag that needs hurdling. The important thing is to stay consistent and keep polishing this game whether or not things are going smoothly or not.

notes.title: More Exercises on the Way in the Next Update Planned for Early May.
notes.notes:
11th April 2020

[b]Boot Camp Fitness Released in Early Access[/b]
First of all, it will be a pleasure and a lot of fun working with you to make this game even better. Thank you for your interest in this game. I will read every comment or review and consider all suggestions carefully. This game will most likely be in Early Access mode for about a year, where more and more exercises will be added and also improvements to the game.

[b]More Exercises Are On The Way[/b]
Any bugs / issues that you find will be given top priority and I will try my best to remedy them ASAP.
For the 1.1 update that is planned for early May, next month, I will concentrate efforts on two main areas:

a) More exercises to make workouts even more varied.

b) The initial exercise (animated sprite) is causing a slight performance hit, making the initial exercise (after the 10 second count down) in the first 1 or 2 seconds, a little glitchy as it loads up. I plan to improve upon this by pre-loading the initial exercise sprite.

Please tell me what you like and don't like about the game, so that I can improve upon the current version even more. Any suggestions for improvements? Or have you come across any bugs?

We can shape this game based upon feedback as to how good you expect this game to be.

I invite you to put your suggestions or constructive criticism in reviews or in comments on the Boot Camp Community page, or to post your results up, or a screenshot of ranks & unlocks you are achieving or anything else fun.

Stay safe,

Kevin

notes.title: Will Try to Release this Game ASAP for People Locked Down Wanting to Exercise.
notes.notes:
Hi, I hope you are well and staying as safe as possible. I know that many people are on 'lock down' within their homes (including myself) so [b]I will try to release this game ASAP[/b]. As so far it is the only non-VR exercise game on Steam where the actual player works out at the time of writing.

Originally I was going to release this game in April 2020, then I decided to move the release date to November 2020 so that I could bring Boot Camp Fitness out totally polished and with every feature I have planned for it. However, that would almost be selfish to delay release at a time when people need exercising at home options, especially players who don't have VR goggles. As keeping fit will not only help us stay healthy in general, but it will no doubt strengthen our immune system to fight back against viruses.

Even though in early access the game is fully playable, it's a full game with 132 exercise variations (including left, right stance variations), with all the features mentioned on the store page enabled. With all exercise levels, times, core exercises, flexibility exercises, strength exercises, location unlocks and rank unlocks are all fully functional. You will get a great workout in. I just want to polish  the game until it is the very best it can be for players. The game will be in early access for around one year, where I'll add exercises to have 300+ exercise variations as well as new features in this time with frequent updates.

I will work around the clock to release the game sometime in April preferably, or May if not - as soon as I can. 

I will release the game as an early access game at 50% of the originally planned price and will act on people's feedback and work with players to make it an even better game.

I will keep the emphasis on adding a lot of new exercises early on in the early access stage. I also have a lot of great update/new feature ideas I want to implement in the game thanks to feedback so far from people.

Please leave me feedback on the community forum about what you like and don't like about this game when it releases. You can help me build this game and we can maybe sucker punch the Corona Virus by way of increasing our health to give it a tougher fight if we are unlucky enough to come down with it.

Of course, I'm not suggesting that working out will protect us from viruses, but wholesome food and regular exercise gives us a lot better immune system to fight them.

Let's emerge from these lockdowns fitter, leaner, and stronger - a virus's worst nightmare when searching for weakness.

Take care of yourself.

Kind regards,
Kevin

notes.title: November 2019 Pre-Release Progress Report
notes.notes:
I was pleasantly surprised to see there are already people who have subscribed to the community group of Boot Camp Fitness, even though it doesn’t unlock until April 16th 2020. So, I thought I’d post a progress report about how the game is progressing.

First of all I’d like to thank Jadranko Duric for his advice on which bodyweight and cardio exercises to include in Boot camp Fitness. Jadranko is a strength and conditioning coach at FC Meyrin with over 10 years experience coaching, who graduated from the Faculty of Kinesiology at the university of Zagreb. Following the advice of professionals such as Jadranko when it comes to which exercises to include and exactly which algorithms (order) to assemble those exercises in lets me concentrate my efforts in the game’s development - aka programming and animating.

So far I’ve completed 40 3D animations of the planned 200+ animations. The game’s interface is solid. So far I have only found 1 bug which I’ve now fixed. All 18 workout locations are up as well as the Boot Camp ranking system. It will be a lot of fun unlocking locations and climbing the ranks as a reward for putting the well earned time into working out regularly.

This month I’ll be focusing mainly on more animations, plus creating the skeleton of the algorithm timing system that will create a unique workout for every workout. For this system I will only focus on coding a flexible framework and then consult with fitness professionals as to what order and exercises it will select for each workout.

 Have a great day :)
